validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, not a GEM-only entity. Multiple independent sources describe this exact segment: neftegaz.ru's 2019 incident report ('взрыв газопровода ... Мастах-Берге-Якутск на 239 км'; lists 'газопровод-подключение Мастах - Берге' as one of the 3 named components of the wider ГТС), Rostekhnadzor's press service via Interfax-Russia (2023-03-03, 'Участке магистрального газопровода СВГКМ-Мастах-Берге-Якутск (I, II, и III нитки)' -- explicitly enumerating threads I/II/III as distinct physical strings under one regulatory designation), and Sakhatransneftegaz's own internal commissioning-year table (image embedded in an ipng.ysn.ru article, visually inspected this run), which lists 'МГ Мастах-Берге, 1 нитка' and 'МГ Мастах-Берге, 2 нитка' as SEPARATE table rows with different lengths and commissioning years. DUPLICATE CHECK: P3364 (this row, thread I, 184.00 km per the table) is NOT a duplicate of sibling P6691 (Mastakh-Berge II) -- the same internal table shows thread II was built in four separate phases (59.00 km/1984, 36.30 km/1986, 51.80 km/1987, 36.70 km/1988; phases sum to ~183.8 km, coincidentally close to thread I's 184.00 km but a genuinely separate physical string with its own distinct construction history -- see cross_row_leads). No relabel/segment-double-count risk found. CLASSIFICATION CAVEAT: neftegaz.ru's system breakdown labels the Mastakh-Berge component a 'газопровод-подключение' (connector/connection pipeline), a narrower Russian technical/administrative term than the 'МГП' (магистральный газопровод, trunk pipeline) label it reserves for the Taas-Tumus-Yakutsk leg specifically. However, Rostekhnadzor -- the actual safety regulator -- classifies the WHOLE corridor including this segment as a 'магистральный газопровод' under one safety-oversight designation ('Участке магистрального газопровода СВГКМ-Мастах-Берге-Якутск'), and the segment is long-haul (184 km), high-pressure, cross-district infrastructure functionally indistinguishable from trunk/transmission pipe. GEM's PipelineType=transmission is kept as correct; the 'connector' label is noted as an internal Russian naming nuance, not a classification error.

validity.recommendation: Keep Capacity=1.50 bcm/y as recorded. Flagging a genuine grammatical ambiguity in the sourcing for the record; recommend cross-checking sibling P6691 (Mastakh-Berge II) -- if it carries the identical 1.50 bcm/y figure, that would support the per-thread reading used here, whereas a materially different figure on P6691 would suggest the underlying prose describes a combined/aggregate 2-thread total that has been applied to both rows and should be revisited.
validity.researcher_notes: neftegaz.ru/194257 states: 'Проектная производительность 2-х ниток - 4,2 млн м3/сутки, максимальная - 6,3 млн м3/сутки, 3-й нитки - около 8 млн м3/сутки.' Converted, 4.2 million m3/day x 0.365 = 1.533 bcm/y, closely matching the recorded 1.50 bcm/y. The Russian is genuinely ambiguous between 'design capacity OF the 2 threads [combined]' and 'design capacity of EACH of the 2 threads' -- the preceding sentence in the same article uses an explicit 'каждая' (each) qualifier for length ('Протяженность - 460 км каждая из 2-х'), which the capacity sentence lacks, weakly favoring a combined reading; however a combined-then-halved figure (~2.1 million m3/day per thread, ~0.77 bcm/y) would sit far below both the recorded value AND the plausible engineering jump to the newer 720mm 3rd thread's ~8 million m3/day (a per-thread reading, 4.2 to 8, is a more physically consistent 720mm-vs-530mm capacity scaling step than a combined-then-halved 2.1 to 8 jump). On balance the per-thread reading is favored and supports the recorded value at medium confidence.
